O.outcome_detail: association with play duration, extra clicks, first-try-correct rate, and total wrong clicks

result.effect: Spearman |ρ| ≤ 0.38; strongest association engagement–extra clicks ρ = -0.38, p = 0.08

cells.quote: Spearman rank correlations between each sub -dimension and the gameplay metrics (duration, extra clicks, first-try-correct rate, total wrong clicks) were all small-to-moderate (|ρ| ≤ 0.38) and none reached the uncorrected p < 0.05 threshold. The strongest tendency was a moderate negative association between engagement and extra clicks (ρ = -0.38, p = 0.08), intuitive but far from confirmatory at this sample size.
cells.note: The study reports exploratory measured associations rather than a manipulated treatment comparison.

O.outcome_detail: Granger-causal neural information flow at CH6–CH14

cells.quote: For the CH6–CH14, a 4 (Group: IF, OF, IC, NF) × 2 (Direction: provider→ receiver, receiver→ provider) mixed-design ANOVA revealed a significant main effect of group (F(3, 96) = 4.951, p = 0.003, η2P = 0.134). Post-hoc comparisons indicated that the IF group (0.0044 ± 0.0045) exhibited significantly higher GCA values than the NF group (0.0014 ± 0.0015; p = 0.002).
cells.note: The study text does not state participant expertise, age, setting, duration, or assignment method.

O.outcome_detail: Granger-causal neural information flow within the one-way feedback group

cells.quote: A significant interaction was also observed (F(3, 96) = 3.065, p = 0.032, η2P = 0.087). Post-hoc tests showed that, in the OF group, GCA values were significantly higher in the provider→ receiver direction (0.0044 ± 0.0032) than in the receiver → provider direction (0.0026 ± 0.0028; p = 0.013).
cells.note: This is a direction contrast within the one-way feedback group; the study text does not state participant expertise, age, setting, duration, or assignment method.

O.outcome_detail: AUT creativity acquisition: fluency, flexibility, and uniqueness

cells.quote: Results indicated a signi ﬁcant interaction effect on creativity scores (ﬂuency, ﬂexibility, and uniqueness; Fs(3, 96) ≥ 4.142, ps ≤ 0.008, η2 Ps ≥ 0.115). Subsequent simple effects analyses revealed that posttest creativity scores in the IF group (ﬂuency: 9.97 ± 3.64;ﬂexibility: 4.64 ± 1.83; uniqueness: 5.08 ± 2.21) were higher than those in the pretest ( ﬂuency: 7.21 ± 2.08;ﬂexibility: 3.80 ± 1.70; uniqueness: 3.59 ± 1.84;ps < 0.001).
cells.note: The study reports a significant Time × Group interaction across the four feedback groups; the quoted simple effects establish improvement within the interpersonal-feedback group, while the detailed posttest comparisons show interpersonal feedback advantages over no feedback for uniqueness acquisition.
